**CYBER THREAT INTELLIGENCE SPRINT | TASK 4**

**Threat actor profile: CyberAv3ngers**

Politically motivated threat group | Prepared for Desert Oil | October 1, 2026

**SUMMARY**

CyberAv3ngers, also tracked as Soldiers of Solomon, is a suspected Iranian group affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). It has been active since at least 2020 and attacks industrial control systems, mostly in Israel and the United States.

A joint federal advisory published on July 24, 2026 reports ongoing exploitation of programmable logic controllers (PLCs) in US critical infrastructure. The 2023 Unitronics campaign mostly defaced controller screens. The 2026 activity has caused confirmed operational disruption and financial losses, and it has expanded beyond Rockwell Automation to Schneider Electric and Siemens equipment.

Saudi Arabia is not a named victim in the data we reviewed. The risk to Desert Oil comes from shared exposure: the group targets energy, water and government operators, and it gets in through internet-exposed controllers, valid credentials and legitimate engineering software.

# 1\. Actor overview

**Name and aliases**

CyberAv3ngers, also tracked as Soldiers of Solomon

**Suspected origin**

Iran. Affiliated with the IRGC (CISA advisory AA23-335A, December 2023)

**Active since**

At least 2020

**Type of group**

State-affiliated APT group

**Primary focus**

Industrial control systems, including PLCs and operator screens, in critical infrastructure

**Confidence in affiliation**

Moderate to high. The affiliation comes from government advisory reporting, and the platform marks the record as confirmed by other sources.

The group did not appear when we searched actor descriptions for the keywords state-sponsored, political and nation-state, because its political context sits in linked reports and not in its own description.

We found it by searching its name, then confirmed it through its description, its campaign and two linked reports.

# 2\. Motivation and objectives

The platform has no motivation value for this group, so we assessed it from the actor description, the targets and the government reporting the platform cites.

-   The platform description says the group made disputed and false claims of critical infrastructure compromises in Israel, and its later targets are in the United States. Together with the IRGC link, this fits a state-directed political aim.
-   The 2023 campaign defaced controller screens. The 2026 activity changes controller logic and manipulates operator displays, and has caused operational disruption and financial losses for victims.
-   The 2023 campaign hit Unitronics controllers worldwide wherever they were exposed. The sources describe that targeting as opportunistic and global.

# 3\. Targets

**Dimension**

**Observed targeting**

**Countries**

Israel, United States

**Sectors**

Government and energy. The 2023 campaign also reached water and wastewater, food and beverage manufacturing and healthcare. The 2026 report adds water facilities.

**Equipment**

Unitronics PLCs with touchscreen interfaces (2023). Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric and Siemens equipment (2026). IP cameras, routers, HMIs, PLCs and firewalls (IOCONTROL).

**Common weakness**

Controllers reachable from the internet, default or weak credentials, and remote engineering access without strong controls

# 4\. Campaigns and timeline

**Date**

**Event**

**Source**

**2020 onward**

Group active. Early claims of critical infrastructure compromises in Israel are described as disputed and false.

CISA AA23-335A, as cited in the platform

**Nov 2023**

Unitronics Defacement Campaign. Opportunistic worldwide intrusions into Unitronics Vision Series PLCs. The most notable effect was defacement of the controller screens (HMIs).

CISA AA23-335A; press reporting (Bajak and Levy)

**Dec 11, 2024**

IOCONTROL report. Analysis of a custom IoT/OT malware family used by Iran-affiliated attackers against Israeli and US devices, believed to be a nation-state cyberweapon aimed at civilian critical infrastructure.

Team82, via AlienVault

**Jul 24, 2026**

Ongoing PLC exploitation advisory. Federal agencies warn of active exploitation of PLCs in US critical infrastructure. Unlike 2023, it has caused confirmed operational disruption and financial losses, and it has expanded beyond Rockwell Automation to Schneider Electric and Siemens.

Joint federal advisory, via AlienVault

# 5\. Tactics and techniques

The platform links 20 MITRE ATT&CK techniques to the group. The table groups them by attack stage.

**Attack stage**

**Techniques**

**How it shows up**

**Reconnaissance**

T1595 Active Scanning

Scans for internet-exposed industrial systems. The July report names ports 22, 102, 502, 2222 and 44818.

**Initial access**

T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application

T1133 External Remote Services

T1078 Valid Accounts

Connects to exposed controllers with valid or default credentials and legitimate engineering software, appearing as an authorized technician.

**Execution and persistence**

T1059.004 Unix Shell

T1053.003 Cron

T1547.006 Kernel Modules and Extensions

IOCONTROL runs arbitrary code and persists by installing a daemon.

**Defense evasion**

T1027, T1027.002 Obfuscation and packing

T1036 Masquerading

T1070.004 File Deletion

T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode

T1497 Sandbox Evasion

Hides the malware and deletes its files. In the 2026 activity, attackers also hide anomalies by manipulating operator displays.

**Discovery**

T1016, T1046, T1082, T1083

Collects system and network details and lists network services and files.

**Command and control**

T1571 Non-Standard Port

T1572 Protocol Tunneling

T1102.002 Web Service

IOCONTROL communicates over the MQTT protocol and uses DNS over HTTPS.

**Impact (report linked)**

T1565.001 Stored Data Manipulation

T1498.001 Direct Network Flood

T1601 Modify System Image

Altered controller logic and operator views. The 2023 campaign lists loss of view, loss of availability, and loss of productivity and revenue.

Techniques linked only to the July 2026 report: T1584.003, T1583.003, T1589.001, T1562.001, T1498, T1205, T1112 and T1078.003.

# 7\. Impact and relevance to Desert Oil

The 2023 campaign showed that Unitronics controllers left exposed to the internet could be taken over around the world. The July 2026 advisory reports that similar access now causes operational disruption and financial loss in US critical infrastructure.

None of the data we reviewed names Saudi Arabia or Saudi Aramco as a victim, so we assess the risk to Desert Oil from shared exposure and not from observed targeting. Oil and gas operators run the same types of controllers, remote engineering access and IT/OT connections that the group exploits, and the platform links the group to the energy sector.

## Recommended actions

-   Inventory every controller and operator screen, and confirm that none is reachable from the internet.
-   Change all default credentials. Require multi-factor authentication and a VPN or jump host for remote engineering access.
-   Block or closely monitor the ports named in the advisory, and alert when engineering software connects from an unexpected location.
-   Separate the corporate network from the control network and limit what can pass between them.
-   Keep offline backups of controller programs, and rehearse running critical processes manually in case operator screens cannot be trusted.
-   Search logs and DNS history for the indicators in section 8.

# 9\. Confidence, gaps and sources

## Limits of this assessment

-   The first seen, last seen and motivation fields are blank on the actor record. Recency comes from linked reports, and motivation is our assessment.
-   The July 2026 report is attributed by correlation in the platform and needs to be checked against the advisory.
-   The platform holds two records for the group, one from MITRE and one from AlienVault. This profile uses the MITRE record as its main source.
-   Saudi Arabia is not listed as a victim, and no incidents or sightings are recorded for the actor.
